status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly state that 'no evidence is presented that the Cdc48 role in this process is direct and it remains possible that Cdc48 affects other aspects of the cell that indirectly lead to this phenotype.' While they acknowledge the quality of the work and the relevance of describing a new role for Cdc48, they indicate that 'mechanistic understanding of this new pathway is missing' and request 'further detailed analyses of the pathway and a better mechanistic understanding.'

Reviewers explicitly state that 'all of the reviewers have credited the quality of the work,' which encompasses the experimental observations showing accumulation of ubiquitinated substrates, tRNA-linked nascent peptides, and reporter proteins in Cdc48 pathway mutants. These observational data are not challenged and form the empirical foundation that reviewers accept.

The claims about Ltn1 and Ubr1 contributing to ubiquitination of substrates on ribosomes are observational findings that are not specifically questioned by reviewers. These fall under the 'quality of the work' that reviewers credited and represent data rather than mechanistic interpretations about directness.

These claims about selective interactions between Cdc48/Ufd1 and non-stop proteins, and accumulation of tRNA-linked forms of specific substrates (GFHNS, PrANS, Gnd1PTC) in mutants represent experimental observations. Reviewers credited the quality of the work and did not challenge these specific findings.

While the differential accumulation patterns between Cdc48 and proteasome mutants are observational data, the interpretation that 'Cdc48 acts upstream of the proteasome' involves mechanistic inference. Given reviewers' concern that 'it remains possible that Cdc48 affects other aspects of the cell that indirectly lead to this phenotype,' the pathway order interpretation is subject to the same uncertainty about directness.
